notes: Tests the drought order process and cross-border Severn regulation in a live drought; the outcome of the Welsh and UK government decisions and any ecological harm on the upper Severn need checking.
summary: The Daily Post reported on 20 August 2026 that NRW had applied to the Welsh Government for a drought order on the River Severn, the first sought for the river in 37 years, after Llyn Clywedog fell below 50 percent capacity, a level NRW called critical. The order would cut Hafren Dyfrdwy's abstraction from the Severn by an initial 5 percent, lower the legal minimum release from the reservoir and cap releases at 300 megalitres a day for up to six months; the Environment Agency applied for a related order in England. NRW said that without it Clywedog releases could cease and parts of the upper Severn could dry, with natural recovery expected within one to three years of normal rainfall.
title: NRW applies for the first River Severn drought order in 37 years as Llyn Clywedog falls below half capacity
